solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very nearly get fair maiden

parts.note: fair means just, as in a just decision
Miss is the title of an unmarried woman, a maiden

explanation.surface: A sly suggestion that someone very nearly won over a pretty young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To just miss something is to fall a hair short of reaching or obtaining it, an idiom for near success.

clue.text: Cursed leading journal's terrible index

indicators.note: leading means the first letter, the one at the front
terrible suggests the word index is in a bad state, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor curses a magazine's awful index.
explanation.definitionFit: Jinxed means under a jinx, affected by bad luck or a curse.

clue.text: Rudely ignores overwhelming victory by English monarch

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so the rearranged letters wrap round the others
rudely means roughly, crudely, so the letters of ignores are rearranged

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign

explanation.surface: An English king rudely snubs others after a crushing victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a supreme ruler, a king or queen reigning over a realm.

clue.text: Claiming career ruined by errors originally in partnership document

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of these words are reworked
originally means at the start, so the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone claims a career was wrecked by errors in a business partnership paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partnership' suggests business, but the partnership here is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage licence is the official permit allowing a couple to wed, legal paperwork for a lifelong union.

clue.text: Woman's getting rare turn as a football pundit

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman; the 's stands for is, a link

indicators.note: turn means twist about, so the letters of rare are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman gets an unusual chance to work as a football commentator.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a former England striker who is now a television football analyst.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Shearer, ex-England captain, is an example of a football pundit on BBC's Match of the Day.

clue.text: Small wound receded with care of plaster

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: receded means drew back, so the word for the wound runs backwards

parts.note: a cut is a wound
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A minor injury that healed with careful treatment, described in medical terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plaster' looks like a sticking plaster for the wound, but it is the wall coating.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used to coat walls and moulded decoration on buildings.

clue.text: Only a small part of the whole lettuce?

definitions.text: Only a small part of the whole lettuce?

parts.words: Only a small part of the whole lettuce?
parts.note: an idiom for a small visible part of a large problem, read literally as the end of an iceberg lettuce

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from icebergs, mostly hidden below water; the question mark flags the lettuce of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a small, evident portion of a much larger hidden whole, and literally the end of an iceberg lettuce.

clue.text: Applaud revolutionary on uprising

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: uprising means going up, and in a down clue that reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Crowds applaud a revolutionary leader during an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer is to shout approval, to applaud someone.

clue.text: Hope is beginning to minimise after work cut hours

indicators.note: after means the following letters come after the work and shortened time

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: hours means time

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Hope is fading as a shortened working week is planned to cut costs.
explanation.walkthrough: TIME cut loses its last letter to give TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimism is hopefulness and confidence about the future.

clue.text: Ancient city quarter involved in plot gets torched

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the city and quarter go within the plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
N, for north, is a compass point or quarter

explanation.surface: A district of an ancient city caught up in a conspiracy is set on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a conspiracy, but it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Burned is the past participle of burn, meaning set on fire, torched.

clue.text: At no time is everyone very content

indicators.note: content as a noun is what something holds, so the answer lies within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A grumble that nobody is ever truly satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as happy, but it is the noun: the contents of the words everyone very.
explanation.definitionFit: Never is the adverb meaning on no occasion whatsoever.

clue.text: Tackle workers engaged in playing piquet

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so the workers sit inside the other letters
playing suggests the card game piquet is being played about with, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: piquet is a card game for two players
men can mean workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Workers on a break absorbed in a game of the card game piquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' reads as a verb but is the noun, as in fishing tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle as a noun is gear or apparatus, the kit needed for a job, such as fishing tackle.

clue.text: Aristocrat taking drug covered by press before

indicators.note: taking means the aristocrat takes on what follows, adding it alongside

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman, an aristocrat

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside, so the drug goes within the word for press

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a nobleman caught taking drugs by the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like it orders the pieces, but it is the definition, an adverb like 'previously'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier on is an adverbial phrase meaning at a previous time, synonymous with before.

clue.text: Conference in favour of union getting money

parts.note: for means in favour of
M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M2 money supply

explanation.surface: A trade-union conference voting for a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting or assembly where ideas are exchanged and discussed.

clue.text: Beginning in Bergen, Grieg developed to be more significant

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
developed means worked into a new form, so the composer's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Grieg, born in Bergen, grew from his start there into a more important composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Edvard Grieg was a Norwegian composer from Bergen.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigger, the comparative of big, can mean of greater importance as well as greater size.

clue.text: Son had trouble cutting back flowers

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read in reverse
cutting means slicing between, so the trouble word goes between the son and had

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A son had difficulty pruning the flowers in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting back flowers' looks like pruning, but 'cutting' and 'back' are separate signals: insert, then read the whole thing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahlias are tuberous garden plants grown for their showy, many-petalled blooms.

clue.text: Chimney within local area has introduced unknown disease

indicators.note: has introduced means has had put into it, so the unknown goes inside the rest
within means inside, so the chimney sits in the pub

parts.note: a local is a British pub, an inn
a flue is a chimney duct
Z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A smoky chimney in the area brought an illness into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a local is a neighbourhood pub. The unknown slips in just before the area letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Influenza, or flu, is a contagious viral illness of the respiratory tract.

clue.text: Understood parking under elevated motorway's legal

indicators.note: under means coming below in a down clue, so the parking follows
elevated means raised, which in a down clue reads the letters upwards, backwards

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
licit means lawful, legal

explanation.surface: A notice explains that parking beneath an elevated motorway is lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit means implied though not stated, understood without being said.

clue.text: Socialises with others in swimming lesson

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside these clue words

explanation.surface: Someone chats and makes friends during a swimming class.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle is to move around a gathering and chat with various people.

clue.text: Good man — eating half of hot sauce in bottle!

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the saint goes around the sauce

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man

indicators.note: half of means only the front half of the sauce's doubled name is kept

parts.note: piri-piri is a hot chilli sauce from Portuguese and African cooking

explanation.surface: A man devouring chilli sauce from a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like the sauce's container, but it is British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, and spirit means courage and mettle too.

clue.text: Centre of anywhere's shoddy and smelly

indicators.note: the centre of an eight-letter word is its two middle letters

parts.note: iffy is informal for of doubtful quality, shoddy

explanation.surface: A complaint that a town centre is run-down and stinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiffy is British informal for having an unpleasant odour, from whiff, a faint smell.

clue.text: Spectator muttered informal greeting

indicators.note: muttered means spoken low, so it is the sound of the greeting that counts

parts.note: wotcher is a British informal greeting, like hello

explanation.surface: A spectator mumbles a casual hello.
explanation.walkthrough: Wotcher is a London slang greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher is an observer, one who looks on as a spectator.

clue.text: Stop fixture in the middle after sides clash

indicators.note: after means the middle letter follows the rearranged letters
clash means collide in disorder, so the letters of sides are rearranged
the middle of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

explanation.surface: A match is halted midway after the two teams start fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' looks like football teams and 'fixture' a match, but each only gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or refrain from an action, to stop.

clue.text: Reason soldier's wearing hair cut short

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the shortened hair goes around the soldier
cut short means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a lock is a tuft of hair
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier's haircut is justified by regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hair cut short' reads as a military crop, but 'cut short' trims the word for a tuft of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, the faculty of thinking things through rationally.

clue.text: Plant a bit of lavender in bark

parts.note: to plant is to grow something

indicators.note: a bit of means just the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Planting a sprig of lavender in tree bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like a tree's skin, but it is a dog's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A growl is a low threatening noise, as a bark is a sound a dog makes.

clue.text: Heartlessly impose oneself, catching bride-to-be with nothing on

indicators.note: catching means taking in, so the shortened word surrounds the bride-to-be
heartlessly means without its heart, so the centre letter of the seven-letter word goes

parts.note: to intrude is to impose oneself on others
a hen is a bride-to-be, as at a hen party before a wedding

explanation.surface: A cruel gatecrasher bursts in on a bride while she is undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is the British bride's pre-wedding celebration, so a hen is a bride-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nude is an idiom meaning naked, wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Comedian's angle on 'Finding Nemo' perhaps

parts.note: a clown is a comedian; the 's stands for has, joining the next word
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A comedian's slant on the Pixar film Finding Nemo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding Nemo' perhaps means the title character Nemo, who is found in the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemo, the hero of the animated film, is an orange-and-white clownfish, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Lethargy and extremes of exhaustion with insulin regularly lacking

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
regularly lacking means every other letter is dropped, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A diabetic feels sluggish and drained when insulin runs short.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and boredom, a feeling of lethargy from lack of interest.

clue.text: Spoke a little bit about love I lost

indicators.note: about means around, so the small amount wraps the other letters

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

indicators.note: lost means the I goes missing from the word

parts.note: to like is close to to love; like as a noun is a fondness

explanation.surface: Someone spoke briefly about a love affair they lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is a verb here, to like, not the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Talked is the past tense of talk, equivalent to spoke as in uttered words.

clue.text: Sweet old lady captured by fine artist with final portrait

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the old lady goes within the other letters

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: final means the last letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: gran is an informal word for grandmother, an old lady

explanation.surface: A sweet old lady is painted by a fine artist in a last portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant means smelling sweet or pleasant, like perfume or flowers.
